findings.reason: The authentic original standalone PNG renders the existing formulas correctly but has no illustration. A paired transition-law schematic materially clarifies the opposing roles of D: absorption fixes each starting point in D, whereas killing preserves its within-D mass and sends its exit mass to a cemetery. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a claim that the original formulas failed to render.

diagram_math_checks.objects_and_domains: K is the probability kernel on (E, mathcal E) of Definition line 27; D is measurable. The absorption diagram is on E. The killing diagram has original states in E and the adjoined cemetery Delta, with the extended sigma-algebra specified in unchanged line 29. Set boxes denote laws on the indicated set, not states or atoms.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Read the complete local definition and supplier def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel: kernel rows are measures, probability rows have total mass one. No finite-state or singleton-measurability assumption is introduced.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Absorption has a mass-one self-loop at each x in D and the unchanged law K(y, dot) from y in D-complement to E.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitution into line 29 gives K_abs(x,A)=1_A(x) for x in D and K_abs(y,A)=K(y,A) for y outside D. The loop denotes the Dirac probability, not a newly assumed atom of K.

diagram_math_checks.relation: For a start x in D, the killing diagram directs the restricted measure K(x, dot intersect D) into D and mass K(x,D-complement) to Delta.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These are exactly the two summands of the first branch of K_kill in line 29. Their masses are K(x,D) and K(x,D-complement), which sum to K(x,E)=1. Both arrows originate at x; no reverse arrows or commutativity claim is made.

diagram_math_checks.relation: An outside start y goes to Delta with mass one, and Delta has a mass-one self-loop.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The second branch of line 29 applies both to y in D-complement and to Delta and equals 1_B(Delta). The native figure visibly contains both incoming arrows and the cemetery loop.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Boundary cases D=E and D=empty agree with the schematic conventions.
diagram_math_checks.justification: For D=E the outside-start node has no instances and K(x,D-complement)=K(x,empty)=0; the within-D law is all of K. For D=empty the inside-start node has no instances; all original starts and Delta go to Delta. This matches unchanged lines 30-32.
